---
title: "Download ADapt"
---

ADapt 0.1.0, the version described in our paper, is on GitHub:
[github.com/sannerlab/adapt](https://github.com/sannerlab/adapt). It runs on **Linux**, in the
Python environment of [ADCP 1.1](../adcp/1.1/download.qmd), with ADFR 0.0.23 and MolKit2 0.0.6.

## 1. Install ADCP 1.1

Follow the [ADCP 1.1 download page](../adcp/1.1/download.qmd). It creates the `adcpsuite`
environment.

## 2. Add ADFR 0.0.23 and MolKit2 0.0.6

They carry the corrections ADapt relies on, and ADCP 1.1 keeps working with them:

```bash
micromamba activate adcpsuite        # or: conda activate adcpsuite
python -m pip install --no-deps --index-url https://sannerlab.github.io/pip/py37/ adfr==0.0.23 molkit2==0.0.6
```

## 3. Get ADapt

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sannerlab/adapt.git
adapt/bin/adapt check                # "ADapt is ready"
```

## 4. Start ADapt

### On your own computer

```bash
adapt/bin/adapt serve --open         # starts ADapt and opens it in your browser
```

Run it again while ADapt is running and it opens a new tab on the same server instead of starting
a second one. The page has a **Quit** button, and ADapt also stops by itself 10 minutes after its
last page was closed. Your sessions are kept: **Recent…** reopens them next time.

### From the desktop (Linux)

The ADapt icon is not installed by default. Add it once, after steps 1 to 3:

```bash
adapt/bin/adapt launcher --desktop   # an ADapt entry in the applications menu and an icon on the desktop
```

A click on the icon does what `adapt serve --open` does: it starts ADapt, or reuses the one already
running, and opens it in your browser. The icon remembers the environment and the output folder
in use when it was made; run the command again if you move ADapt or the environment. Its messages
go to `~/.adapt/server.log`. On GNOME, right-click the desktop icon once and choose **Allow
Launching**. Leave out `--desktop` for the menu entry alone; `adapt/bin/adapt launcher --remove`
takes both away.

### On a remote machine

On a computing cluster or another machine you reach through SSH, start ADapt there and open it from
your own computer:

```bash
adapt/bin/adapt serve                # on the remote machine; prints the address to open
ssh -L 8766:127.0.0.1:8766 <host>    # on your computer; then open the printed address
```

The [documentation](documentation.qmd) has the details.
